second_order: turning insults into April Fools riffs
theme_note: These turns jointly turn an insult into an April Fools exchange; what varies is whether the reply names April Fools, answers mock-seriously, or escalates with a stock sexual line.

second_order: saying an April Fools prank is prepared
theme_note: This single code anticipates a prepared prank but does not identify what it became, so it belongs with no more specific practice.

second_order: calling people to draw Monokuma and showing them where
theme_note: These codes recruit drawing work and make it actionable with coordinates or a reference; calls range from asking whether the room will appear to expanding a head into a full sprite.

second_order: reporting a Discord-made Monokuma back to Reddit
theme_note: These passages carry one off-platform decision back to the room through attribution, helper credits, directions, and screenshots; they vary in what part of the completed work they make visible.

second_order: pitching in pixel work
theme_note: Both codes describe personally adding to the shared drawing; one offers another addition after finishing an avatar and the other reports work already under way.

second_order: calling the drawing done and celebrating it
theme_note: These codes announce, marvel at, or celebrate completion; within the practice, some call it done, some qualify it as nearly or mostly finished, and one swears off repeating the effort.

second_order: using blue to shelter Monokuma
theme_note: These codes propose, continue, question, and explain a blue surround as protection; what varies is whether blue is a practical shield, an unfinished task, or a tactic needing explanation.

second_order: repairing and defending through griefing
theme_note: These passages hold together as continuing repair and defence against overwriting; they vary from uncertainty about survival and urgent calls to fixing pixels, rebuilding slowly, thanking defenders, and naming protection duty.

second_order: threatening to destroy the drawing
theme_note: This single code is an explicit opposing action and does not belong inside the participants' repair practice.

second_order: trying to put r/danganronpa above Monokuma
theme_note: These codes coordinate a subreddit banner through permission, lettering, a design, and a linked plan; outcomes vary from independent work and a reported swastika failure to renewed advertising plans.

second_order: building Monomi beside Monokuma
theme_note: These codes work on Monomi's parts and joke about the cut-off result; the shared practice is extending the room's canvas work to a second character.

second_order: switching underwear flairs on and off for April Fools
theme_note: Moderator passages perform the subreddit-level joke by announcing, explaining, and later reversing the flair change; the shift from claimed permanence to restoration is variation within that performance.

second_order: recognising and showing off underwear flairs
theme_note: Members participate by identifying garments and characters, joking through the pairings, rating them, calling a roll, and claiming credit; their uses vary from recognition to playful self-presentation.

second_order: praising and asking to keep the underwear flairs
theme_note: These codes approve the prank, thank or bless the moderators, and ask that the flairs remain; enthusiasm ranges from a brief compliment to treating the joke as a memorable first subreddit April Fools.

second_order: questioning or rejecting the underwear flairs
theme_note: These codes resist or cannot access the joke by going without flair, questioning the claimed email or the reason for underwear, reacting incredulously, reporting an app limitation, or asking for normal flairs back.

second_order: calling the room r/danganpantyraid
theme_note: These two turns invent and endorse a joke name for the underwear-flair version of the subreddit.

second_order: building Chihiro beside Monokuma
theme_note: This single code recruits help for a distinct character build and fits neither the Monokuma call nor the already-established Monomi work.

second_order: turning the improvement series into April Fools posts
theme_note: These posts recruit an established recurring format for the room's joke, once through Fire Extinguisher-kun and once by turning the format onto its organiser.

second_order: keeping the Re:Birth joke growing
theme_note: These codes explain, share, discuss, and predict further life for the expanding Re:Birth April Fools creation; what varies is whether people make pixel art, headcanons, or anticipate a real continuation.

second_order: working around neighbours and no-touch promises
theme_note: These passages negotiate coexistence around nearby art through acknowledging overlap, recalling promises, yielding space, apologising, maintaining rather than covering, weighing banners, and asking permission; participants differ over how much space neighbours need but repeatedly make restraint explicit.

second_order: centralising place-building talk
theme_note: This single code creates one discussion thread to reduce repeated r/place posts, a coordination practice distinct from any one drawing plan.

second_order: visiting and helping between neighbouring communities
theme_note: One code records an AceAttorney visitor arriving after finding the art and the other answers that community's request for help; the shared practice is crossing subreddit boundaries around neighbouring canvas work.

second_order: roleplaying as Monokuma for April Fools
theme_note: This single code describes sustaining a Monokuma role for the whole day outside the canvas episode.

second_order: asking for a wall against place nonsense
theme_note: This single code rejects rather than joins the event talk and therefore remains a one-code theme.

second_order: automating Kirigiri onto the canvas
theme_note: This single code shares a script intended to place Kirigiri automatically, a method not reducible to ordinary calls for pixel help.

second_order: calling for help and proposing more character art
theme_note: These codes mobilise additional canvas work beyond the original Monokuma through generic help calls, a Kirigiri build, saving Naegi, and a Hifumi proposal; they vary between urgent defence and suggesting what to add next.

second_order: choosing community work over an automated script
theme_note: This single code explicitly contrasts a recalled automation method with working on Kirigiri as a community.

second_order: arguing whether Sonic is dead
theme_note: These three adjacent turns dispute whether building Kirigiri means abandoning Sonic and answer that Sonic either died long ago or never dies.

second_order: reacting to flags covering the art
theme_note: These codes report flags over Monokuma and Kirigiri and answer with anger, a blocked memorial observation, and a despair joke; unlike negotiated coexistence, no settlement with the named builders appears here.

second_order: inspecting damage after Place ended
theme_note: These passages keep checking the finished canvas by identifying one persistent purple pixel, invoking a broken alliance, mourning the banner, answering with distrust, and recounting repeated corrections; the shared practice is qualifying what survived after placement stopped.

second_order: joking about Kirigiri's final neighbours
theme_note: These codes treat Kirigiri's position beside LOLI and HENTAI signs as fitting and wish for a Naegiri heart; they play with the final layout rather than organise further pixels.
